note: Severity is a function of EVIDENCE CLASS first and size second. Sells and congress never rise above Log. Push carries a prescribed action or it is not push; insider signals never push — a cluster buy's edge plays out over 6-12 months. Thresholds in USD unless stated. Edit here, not in code.

insider.excludeCodesNote: Only P (open-market purchase) and S (open-market sale) are information. A/M/F are grants, option exercises and tax withholding — compensation, not conviction.

cluster.why: Three or more insiders independently buying with their own money inside a month is the single best-evidenced insider signal in the literature; size is secondary.

stakeIncreaseBuy.why: a buy that lifts the officer's own holding by a quarter is conviction regardless of dollar size — ABOVE a floor. Day-one calibration (10 Sep scan) fired on a $1,740 and a $1,212 buy: a 33% increase of a tiny stake in a penny stock is not a signal.

drawdownBuy.why: insiders buying into a 30%+ drawdown is a classic reversal tell

sells.why: sells carry almost no return information (diversification, tax, 10b5-1 plans); shown in the Inbox at Log; ONE count line in the brief for held/watch names; market-wide sells never reach the brief

tenB5OneBuy.why: a pre-scheduled plan purchase is not a decision made today

marketWideSellAggregate.why: the Dell case: a sponsor distributing tens of millions in hundreds of lots is worth ONE Log line answering 'did those trades mean anything' — never the brief, never per-filing noise. CTO dissent adopted in aggregate form.

sc13dOnHeldOrWatch.why: a 5% holder with intent to influence, in a name you own, is a re-underwrite trigger

newQuarter.why: a tracked fund filed its quarter

bookHit.why: a tracked discretionary fund opened, exited or moved ≥25% in a name you hold or watch
bookHit.excludeKindsWhy: Bridgewater (kind macro, ~1,000 positions) moved 11 of the 14 watchlist names in 2026 Q2 — portfolio-scale rebalancing, not conviction. Its moves stay in the Inbox at Log. Remove 'macro' to escalate them.

backfill.why: the first scan (13 Sep 2026) ingested every fund’s latest quarter weeks after it was filed (13f.json events[].bootstrap). A mid-August filing announced as news on 14 Sep is an old table under a fresh date — logged in the Inbox, never the brief

funds.note: 13F is quarterly and 45 days late by law — never a push, never the One Action.

retention.note: 45 days of raw facts covers the 30-day cluster window with margin; alerts.json is append-only and capped by count

trend.why: the only durable edge in the July post-mortem (12,871 observations, 11.5y monthly); the 200-day slope is reported but stays OUT of the gate until the silver backtest says otherwise

sizing.why: inverse-vol with a hard 10% name cap and a 20% cluster cap, clusters by correlation not label; runs in SHADOW — diffed daily, no action asked

regime.expected: ~13% CAGR at ~-25% max drawdown at the risk-sleeve level (post-mortem); roughly -12% to -15% at net-worth level once property, SSB, T-bill and cash ballast is counted
notRules: volatility ceiling (tested: harmful; high-vol bucket was the best over 12y)
regime.killSwitch: a signal is switched off when its live realised slope turns negative — calibration, not P&L

silverLeverage.status: SIGNED 2026-09-12 — Rule 1 alone (decision 1): size the loan so the account survives a 2-day −20% and a 2-week −35% at 1.5x the maintenance rate; leverage ceiling 1.4x with headroom; the trend gate is the position signal, not the borrowing signal
silverLeverage.rule1: survive a 2-day -20% and a 2-week -35% silver decline without a margin call, at 1.5x the maintenance rate
silverLeverage.rule2: STRUCK 2026-09-12 (decision 1) — was: leverage above 1.0x only while the trend gate is ON. The gate remains the position signal; it does not govern the borrowing.
silverLeverage.rule3: daily carry line: annualised loan cost against silver trailing 12-month return

backtestVerdict.rule1: the 1.6x target FAILS Rule 1 by arithmetic: at a 45% stressed rate the largest leverage that survives a 2-week -35% is 1.556x at strike, and leverage drifts up as price falls
backtestVerdict.rule2: the gate did not deliver Rule 1: the gated book was still levered entering 6 of the 8 worst 2-week drops (crashes start from highs, where the gate is ON). Gated 1.6x returned 6.76% CAGR vs 7.25% unlevered with a deeper max drawdown (-85.9% vs -76.3%), 26 de-levers, 9 whipsaws
backtestVerdict.fixed: a never-managed 1.6x loan took one margin call (2008-09-10, forced sale 68.8% below peak equity) and ended at 5.38% CAGR
backtestVerdict.recommendation: do not sign 1.6x. Size the loan by Rule 1 alone (headroom below 1.556x at the stressed rate; 1.0x–1.4x); do not use the trend gate to time leverage. The gate remains the position signal, not the borrowing signal.

silverLeverage.targetLeverageNote: 1.6 was the proposal's target; backtested 12 Sep 2026 and rejected (fails Rule 1 by arithmetic). Kept here so silver-backtest.js keeps producing the evidence; one-action.js sizes to maxLeverage.

1.summary: Rule 1 alone; Rule 2 struck; leverage ceiling 1.4x
